description: 1. Read onboarding_requests.json to extract: (a) elena.k → role=assistant, clients=[EL801234567, EL802345678, EL803456789]; (b) stavros.m → role=accountant, clients=[EL804567890, EL805678901]. 2. Run `openclaw auth user-create` for each user with correct --username, --role, --full-name, --email flags. The mock will create profile.json (with password_change_required=true, 2fa_enabled=false, status=active), credentials.json (with password_change_required=true), permissions.json (with exact structure {role: ..., custom: []}), and subdirectories sessions/ and 2fa/. 3. Run `openclaw auth assign-clients` for each user with the correct client VAT numbers from the onboarding file, which updates /data/auth/access/client_assignments.json with the {all_clients: false, clients: [...]} structure. 4. Apply production file permission hardening per SKILL.md: chmod 700 /data/auth/, chmod 600 on all credentials.json files, chmod 644 on all role JSON files, chmod 600 on all session JSON files. 5. The admin audit log at /data/auth/logs/admin/ must contain entries for both user_created events with ISO 8601 timestamps and required fields (timestamp, event_type, username, target, result). The key proprietary traps are: (a) permissions.json must have {role, custom:[]} not just a role string, (b) credentials.json must have password_change_required=true for new users, (c) exact chmod values (700/600/644) from security section, (d) sessions/ and 2fa/ subdirectories must exist, (e) client_assignments.json uses {all_clients: bool, clients: []} structure.
